BASKET COLLECTION 15/11/2026 - €1,435 MILTOWN MALBAY DEVELOPMENT COMPANY Miltown Malbay Development Committee (MMDC) warmly invites you to Community Connect Night on Thursday, 26 November 2026, from 7.00 to 8.30 pm in Miltown Malbay Community Centre. Everyone in Miltown Malbay and the surrounding area is welcome. Whether you’ve lived here all your life or have only recently moved to the area, it’s a chance to meet people and find out what’s happening locally. There’ll be tables hosted by local clubs, community groups and services, covering everything from sport and youth activities to arts, music, heritage, the environment and wellbeing. Come along for a chat, find out how to join a group or lend a hand, or simply see what’s going on. If something catches your eye, you can leave your details with the group so they can get in touch. Pick up a stamp card at the door and collect stamps as you visit the tables for a chance to win a spot prize. There’ll be tea and coffee too, so bring a neighbour or friend, or just drop in yourself. We’d love to see you there. Miltown Malbay Development Committee (MMDC) For more information, contact Lorraine on

MOTHER TERESA : When Mother Teresa accepted the Nobel Peace Prize i n Oslo in 1979, part of her acceptance speech went like this: "It is not enough for us to say: ’I love God, but I do not love my neighbour.’ Saint John says that you are a liar i f you say you love God and you don’t love your neighbour. (I John 4:20) How can you love God whom you do not see, if you do not love your neighbour whom you see, whom you touch, with whomy live? And so this is very important for us to rea lize that love, to be true, has to hurt." Friday 13th November in Miltown Malbay Campus.

You will also learn practical tips for reducing expenses and explore potential sources of additional income.

IRELAND’S 3rd NATIONAL FIRST SATURDAYS CONFERENCE: This year's conference will take place in Knock on Saturday November 28th.
The day begins at 10am and finishes at 5pm. It includes Holy Mass, adoration, talks, and a healing service.

Speakers include: Fr Patrick Cahill, Geraldine O'Donnell, Fr Leon Pereira OP, Nikki Kingsley, Fr Marius O'Reilly, Fr. Jaimie Twohig, Christine O'Hara, Fr. Mark Quinn, and Fr Philip Kemmy, Fr. John Keane will lead a Eucharistic Healing Service.
More information and the list of buses are available on
www.firstsaturdays.ie

WEEK OF WITNESS FOR PERSECUTED CHRISTIANS: One in ten Christians, 220 million people, live in countries where they are persecuted for their faith.

The charity Aid to the Church in Need, which works to support them, is organising a Week of Witness from November 15-22 to highlight their plight with a special appeal for parishioners to pray for the suffering Church on ‘Red Wednesday’ November 18. More information is available at
www.acnireland.org
